bug_description.original: Detailed report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5721515274797056 Project: skia Fuzzer: afl_skia_api_raster_n32_canvas Fuzz target binary: api_raster_n32_canvas Job Type: afl_asan_skia Platform Id: linux Crash Type: Heap-use-after-free READ 4 Crash Address: 0x6040000003e0 Crash State: SkPath::reverseAddPath FuzzPath FuzzPath Sanitizer: address (ASAN) Recommended Security Severity: High Regressed: https://oss-fuzz.com/revisions?job=afl_asan_skia&range=201809120304:201809130306 Reproducer Testcase: https://oss-fuzz.com/download?testcase_id=5721515274797056 Issue filed automatically.
bug_description.normalized: OSS-Fuzz issue 10318: skia heap-use-after-free (READ 4) reported by the afl_skia_api_raster_n32_canvas fuzzer. Crash state SkPath::reverseAddPath <- FuzzPath <- FuzzPath. The self-referential path->reverseAddPath(*path) aliases the destination and source SkPathRef; a growForVerb realloc during the reverse walk frees the shared fConicWeights buffer that is then read.

source.description: Fuzzer input is materialized into the SkPath here: a fuzz-selected op builds a rounded rectangle from fuzzer-controlled floats, whose rounded corners are emitted as conic verbs. This allocates and populates the SkPathRef fConicWeights SkTDArray<float> heap buffer that is later aliased, freed and read (the ASan-reported 24-byte region).
source.value_from: Untrusted AFL/fuzzer byte stream (Fuzz data buffer from OSS-Fuzz testcase 5721515274797056): fuzz->nextRange op selector plus fuzz_nice_float(a,b) corner radii and the SkRect r feeding path->addRoundRect.

sink.description: Heap-use-after-free READ of size 4: *--conicWeights dereferences a pointer into src's fConicWeights float buffer after a this->conicTo() growForVerb realloc has freed that same buffer, because src aliases *this. ASan crash at src/core/SkPath.cpp:1748:47.

root_cause.description: reverseAddPath does not detect that the source path aliases *this. It captures raw end pointers (pts, verbs, conicWeights) into src->fPathRef and then appends the reversed verbs to this->fPathRef. When this==src (e.g. op 26 path->reverseAddPath(*path)), a growForVerb realloc during the reverse walk frees the very buffer those raw pointers still iterate over. The fix adds an 'if (this == src)' guard that deep-copies src into a temporary SkPath (SkTLazy<SkPath> tmp) before constructing the Editor.

parser_admitted.note: The fuzzer byte stream is decoded into SkPath op codes and admitted into the path-op interpreter; on a later iteration op 26 (path->reverseAddPath(*path)) is selected, entering the vulnerable self-add path. Earlier than root cause/sink, later than the harness entry.

tainted_value_origin.description: Raw pointer to the end of src's fConicWeights SkTDArray<float> heap buffer. Because src==*this, this is the same buffer that this->conicTo() reallocates during the reverse walk, so conicWeights becomes dangling and is dereferenced by *--conicWeights.

coarse_trace.summary: Fuzzer entry hands the raw testcase bytes to fuzz_RasterN32Canvas.
Sets up the RasterN32 canvas fuzz driver and dispatches canvas ops.
Decodes a canvas op that builds a fuzzed SkPath via FuzzPath.
Recursively builds a child SkPath (FuzzPath, maxOps-1) driven by fuzzer bytes.
Op 26 selected: path->reverseAddPath(*path) self-add on a path that already contains conic (rounded-rect) verbs.
this->conicTo() reallocates the aliased fConicWeights buffer, then *--conicWeights reads freed memory (HUAF READ 4).

fine_trace.note: Fuzz-selected op 19 builds a rounded rectangle from fuzzer floats; the rounded corners are emitted as conic verbs, allocating/growing the SkPathRef fConicWeights SkTDArray<float> heap buffer that becomes the tainted object.

fine_trace.code: this->conicTo(...);  // rounded-corner conic appends a weight
fine_trace.note: Each rounded corner is appended via conicTo, growing fConicWeights through SkPathRef::growForVerb -> SkTDArray<float>::append -> sk_realloc_throw. This is the 24-byte SkTDArray<float> region ASan later reports as freed-then-read (allocation stack: addRoundRect -> addRRect -> conicTo -> growForVerb).
A later fuzz op selects case 26, invoking reverseAddPath with the path as both destination and source. This is the taken control branch that establishes the this==src aliasing.
MISSING guard: the vulnerable code has no 'if (this == src)' aliasing check before editing this->fPathRef, so src->fPathRef IS this->fPathRef. The fix inserts the deep-copy guard here.
Captures a raw end pointer into src's fConicWeights buffer. Because src==*this, conicWeights aliases the same heap buffer that this->conicTo() will realloc.

Appending the first reversed conic's weight, this->conicTo() -> SkPathRef::growForVerb -> SkTDArray<float>::resizeStorageToAtLeast -> realloc grows this->fConicWeights. Since src aliases this, the src weights buffer is freed and the conicWeights pointer (into src) now dangles (free stack: reverseAddPath -> conicTo -> growForVerb -> realloc).

On a following conic verb of the reverse walk, *--conicWeights dereferences the dangling pointer into the freed 24-byte SkTDArray<float>, producing the ASan heap-use-after-free READ of size 4 at src/core/SkPath.cpp:1748:47.

format.name: Skia RasterN32 canvas fuzzer op stream (afl_skia_api_raster_n32_canvas)
format.contract: Raw byte stream consumed by FuzzRasterN32Canvas/FuzzPath as a sequence of SkPath op selectors and floats. To be reachability-comparable a candidate must (1) decode to a valid SkPath op sequence that first builds a path containing at least one conic verb (e.g. addRoundRect / addRRect / addOval rounded corners) so fConicWeights is non-trivially allocated, and (2) subsequently select the self-referential reverse-add op (op 26 -> path->reverseAddPath(*path)) so that this==src aliasing drives a growForVerb realloc of the shared conic-weights buffer during the reverse walk. Exact byte values are not required; the op-dispatch admission and the build-conics-then-self-reverse-add ordering are the reachability contract.
